messages:
maria: Observed a sharp p95/p99 spike on hosted API around 10:12 UTC, looks localized to a handful of workers in us-west. p50 OK, p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~2.3s. Queue depth on those hosts climbed to 200+.
aj: Which worker group / kernel variant? Any recent rollouts?
maria: Affected pods: runtime-prod-usw-6{2..5}. Kernel selector logs show a lot of switches to `kernel_v2_slow_path` around spike start. No infra deploys at that time (checked deploy-bot). Perf graphs attached in thread (see perf-bot below).
zach: Could be batching heuristic misfiring — if short-seq optimizer keeps deferring batching we can hit a tail. Anyone seen KV cache churn?
maria: KV cache hit ratio dropped from 82% -> 45% on those pods. Eviction rate spiked. Tenant mix shows a couple heavy embedding clients on same hosts.
perf-bot: Snapshot of relevant metrics (10:05-10:20 UTC): `p95=1.1s, p99=2.3s, queue_depth_avg=142, kvcache_hits=45%, batch_size_median=1.1, kernel_fallback_rate=18%`
aj: Can you paste the kernel selector debug lines? Need to see the heuristic decisions.
maria: paste below:
```
[10:11:58] kernel_selector: seq_len=24 predicted_batch=16 -> select kernel_v1_fast
[10:11:59] kernel_selector: seq_len=12 predicted_batch=2 -> select kernel_v2_slow_path (fallback)
[10:12:03] kernel_selector: kernel_latency_estimate mismatch, switching to v2 for safety
[10:12:05] kernel_selector: kernel_v2 fallthrough due to warmup_timeout
```
kevin: Warmup timeout? That hints at priming logic failing when load pattern changes. Maybe batching sampler didn't prime KV cache/prefetch for the hot tenant.
sumi: If KV hit ratio drops, priming/prefetch thresholds were probably too conservative. We recently tightened `prefetch_concurrency` in config-2026-02-18, could be related.
aj: Good call. Any noisy neighbor on those nodes? I/O or GPU saturation from embeddings jobs?
maria: GPU util ~60% but memory pressure small. There's one tenant doing high-rate short embeddings bursts every 2s on same hosts. We throttle at route level but bursts still queue locally.
kevin: Quick mitigation: rotate those tenants off the affected hosts (live-move) or bump ratecap per-route to relieve queueing. Which is faster?
zach: Live-move requires placement churn; rolling route ratecap up by 2x for the tenant is faster to test.
maria: I'll patch a temporary ratecap tweak and reobserve.
deploy-bot: rollout started: config/ratecaps/tenant-embeddings-ttl -> +2x on prod-usw targeting runtime-prod-usw-62..65
maria: After bump: p95 back to ~150ms within 40s, p99 down to ~320ms. Kernel fallback rate dropped from 18% -> 2%. KV hit ratio creeping back up to 70%.
sumi: That confirms pressure from tenant priming/queueing causing kernel selector to fall back. We should adjust prefetch_concurrency and sampler priming windows.
aj: Action items:
- maria: keep ratecap tweak for 30m, collect detailed traces (kv evictions, kernel decisions) (ETA 1h)
- sumi: revert tight prefetch change in staging and run the priming benchmark (ETA 2d)
- kevin: add an alert for kernel_fallback_rate > 5% + queue_depth > 100 on a host (ETA today)
- zach: evaluate placement isolation for high-rate embedding tenants (follow-up meeting)
kevin: Also add a short-term heuristic: if kvcache_hit < 60% and batch_size_median < 2 => favor v1_fast until priming recovers.
aj: Sounds good. We should file a retro ticket with timeline and include the sampled profiler output.
maria: attaching small async profiler snippet (sampling, showing time in kernel_v2 path):
```
kernel_v2_slow_path: 48%
kernel_v1_fast: 22%
batching_overhead: 18%
kv_eviction_work: 12%
```
zach: Nice. Once we have the staging run for the prefetch revert, we can tune prefetch_concurrency and priming timeout. For now, leaving ratecap bump in place and monitoring.
maria: Will monitor for 2 hours and then either rollback ratecap or keep if stable. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
